question: The ordinary reviewer can recruit an observed extra model. Can it also decide from measured feedback to remove a redundant existing voter, saving external resources without hurting accuracy?
choices: Use the four-member allocation actually elected, and the same two saved five-fold probability archives, one frozen predictor set per fold. On each held fold, partition by deterministic SHA256('B remove voter v1/'+shared-group) modulo 3. Rotate three group-disjoint roles, assessing each row exactly once. Nominate either the unchanged vote or the removal of exactly one member with other weights proportionally renormalized. Maximize nomination accuracy, then minimize uncompressed distinct external file bytes, then number of component calls, then a hash of nomination probabilities. Compute bytes from dependency manifests of fitted component models, counting a shared file once. Each training run was blind to all three roles of its own held fold.
check: On a separate confirmation role accept a removal only if it matches or exceeds incumbent accuracy. On the third role count all fixes and losses and the number of rows served with fewer components/unique weight bytes. Repeat for both predeclared assignments irrespective of sign. Do not use audit answers to decide which member to remove.
promotion: Consider a live trial for accuracy if both assignments are nonnegative and at least one gains 0.20 percentage points. Independently consider it for efficiency if the cluster-bootstrap 95% lower bound of accuracy difference exceeds -0.30 percentage points in both, and average external weight bytes fall by at least 15% in both. File size is a dependency estimate, never measured latency. These are development simulations of a decision, not new course scores.
budget: Zero fitted models and zero model requests. No designated validation, test or H2. Reuse measured fold results; report both assignments on the same 8301 training examples separately.
